name: SVG Path Particle Reveal
useWhen: A project needs an SVG silhouette, line-art path, moon, constellation, route, icon, or logo mark to scatter from depth and assemble into a premium particle shape.
source: User-provided JavaScript snippet that samples an SVG path with getTotalLength/getPointAtLength, creates THREE.Vector3 vertices, jitters them in x/y/z, and animates them from a centered origin with a GSAP timeline.
implementationNotes: Use owned, generated, open-source-permitted, or user-provided SVG paths only.
Normalize the SVG viewBox before mapping vertices into the scene; the captured 600 by 552 origin only applies to matching artwork.
For production Three.js, render sampled points with BufferGeometry and THREE.Points rather than one mesh per point.
Tune point density by device class; the captured 0.1 path step is dense and may be too heavy for mobile.
Use as a cinematic hero, loader, ambient background, logo reveal, or transition, not as critical navigation.
Keep source-video headings and code frames out of the preview UI; code belongs in files and metadata.
reducedMotion: Render the final path or logo as a static particle/shape image, skip the scatter timeline, and do not delay access to page content.
avoid: blocking auth, checkout, or data-entry flows
text placed directly on dense bright particles
visible code panels inside the design preview
